key_insight: Generalized hydrodynamic stability analysis captures rarefaction effects missed by Navier–Stokes theory, revealing weakened acoustic–viscous mode synchronization and eventual stabilization of high-speed plane Couette flow.
engineering_relevance: The method supports stability assessment of high-speed rarefied shear flows relevant to high-altitude applications where continuum models lose accuracy.
method: Develop temporal linear stability analysis using 13-moment generalized hydrodynamic equations with slip boundary conditions.
Compare against nonlinear coupled constitutive relation and Navier–Stokes stability formulations.
Evaluate rarefaction effects on base flows, eigenspectra, mode synchronization and disturbance growth.
evidence_signal: Across Ma = 2.5–10 and Kn = 2.7×10⁻⁵–0.07, GHE base-flow predictions agree well with DSMC, while stability predictions differ considerably from Navier–Stokes at Kn of order 0.01.
watch_item: DSMC agreement reported in the abstract validates base-flow profiles, not disturbance growth rates; conclusions are scoped to temporal stability of near-continuum plane Couette flow.
paper_title: A linear stability method based on generalized hydrodynamics: application to high-speed plane Couette flow beyond continuum regime
